meâ posuisse manu, meque[?] datam spem impleturum per coër-
citionem hostium, quando ego id oportunum fore
arbi-trabor: ergo de felici rerum eventu esto securus; quia
in meâ est potestate: nec esto nimis festinus, quia
in meo res fita est arbitrio. Revocatur hic locus ad praxin
à Paulo Hebr. 10: 30. Rom. 12 : 19, in quantum
completitur universalem veritatem, seu canonem decen-
tiæ divinæ, in regimine mundi servandæ: qui dictat ulcis-
cendi partes prorsus divinas esse, supremo Judici solum
committendas, quas ut nemo temere sibi sumere
debet, ita nec cum Deo de ejus exercitio disceptare; sed
in ejus arbitrio plane acquiescendum esse, ut hoc solo
sic contentus, quod Deus noverit & hoc opus suum facere
in tempore.
Et retributio. Verbum שׁלם[?] solvere significat
Lev. 5: 24. & rependere Jud. 1: 7. Nimirum mala
malis, & bona bonis, quod est justitiæ divinæ, quam
Deus abnegare non potest; quippe Judex totius terræ,
Gen. 18: 25, cujus est unicuique compensare pro
opera-bus, Rom. 2: 5. Exponit Deus decretum suum,
& constantem suam voluntatem de dandâ hostibus eccle-
siæ retributione, & abrumpendâ aliquandò suâ tole-
rantiâ, quâ in hostium permissione fuerat usus, quan-

page.notes: Line-initial „ marks of the quotation (ditto marks at the start of each line in "vides di-ploma" to "arbitrio") are shown as one opening quote. The asterisk marks before the side-notes and the small mark before "trabor" are printed signs, not text. Hebrew שׁלם, עת and לעת are doubtful in vowels and dots and are marked [?]. "meque" is doubtful and marked [?]. The side-notes at left are italic run-in notes; their placement in the margin is inferred from their position beside the text. The catchword "tuni-" stands alone at the right below the last line. Signature X at the left foot.
